affectedCopies: Compliance obligation library and detail surfaces (/compliance/obligations)

privacyAssessment.dataSubjectRights: not-applicable — the new columns hold a duration in days and a list of retention-category names on an obligation row; they describe a regulator's rule, not a person
privacyAssessment.reviewDisposition: No data-subject workflow is introduced. The effect on subjects is that some records are kept LONGER, never shorter: floors only lengthen a window. A shorter statutory maximum (storage limitation) is a separate concept the lifecycle algebra already distinguishes and this change does not touch.

migration.name: 20260912060000_obligation_retention_minimum
migration.backfill: Additive. retentionMinimumDays is NULL on every existing row, which reads as 'this obligation states no retention minimum' — true of every obligation seeded before this migration, whose durations existed only as prose. retentionFloorBuckets defaults to the empty array. No existing row changes meaning and no retention window moves until a seed populates a value; because floors only lengthen, a NULL can never shorten retention.
migration.rollback: Forward-only. A corrective migration would drop both columns; nothing else references them, and the retention sweep treats their absence as 'no obligation floors'.

changes.lifecycleDisposition: Obligation is a regulated compliance record (retention=retained in its schema tag) and stays so; these columns add configuration to an existing retained row and are removed only with it. They are read by the retention sweep at run time and never copied elsewhere.

fields.reason: The structured form of a duration the obligation already states in prose. Without it the retention engine cannot read what a regulator requires, which is why floors were hardcoded in a TypeScript table keyed by a hand-maintained industry alias.
fields.provenance: BI-69C29492; spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-08-data-lifecycle-stewardship-convergence-design.md §5 slice 6; obligation-floors.test.ts parity proof

fields.reason: Which retention categories the minimum binds (audit, chat, telemetry). Empty means every category, so an under-specified regulator rule is read broadly rather than narrowly.
